description: Restrictions on what authenticated users are allowed to do are not properly enforced. Attackers can access other users' accounts, view sensitive files, modify data, or change access rights by manipulating IDs, tokens, or URLs.

test_patterns.name: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
test_patterns.method: reference an object ID belonging to another user/account and check whether the API still serves or mutates it
test_patterns.payload_template: Swap the resource ID in the URL/body for one owned by a different account, keep the current user's auth token

test_patterns.name: Forced browsing / missing function-level auth
test_patterns.method: call an admin-only or elevated endpoint with a low-privilege token
test_patterns.payload_template: Send the request with a standard user token against an endpoint expected to require admin role

description: Sensitive data is exposed due to weak or missing encryption in transit or at rest, or because it leaks through verbose error messages, logs, or headers.

test_patterns.name: Sensitive data in error responses
test_patterns.method: trigger a server error (invalid ID, malformed payload) and inspect the response body for stack traces, SQL, or PII
test_patterns.payload_template: Request a resource with an out-of-range or malformed ID and inspect the 4xx/5xx body

description: Untrusted input is passed to an interpreter (SQL, NoSQL, OS command, LDAP) as part of a command or query, allowing an attacker to alter the intended query or execute unintended commands.

test_patterns.name: SQL Injection via query/body parameter
test_patterns.method: inject SQL metacharacters/tautologies into string parameters and compare response size/content against a baseline request

test_patterns.name: Command injection via filename/path parameter
test_patterns.method: inject shell metacharacters into parameters that may reach a filesystem or shell call

description: Missing or ineffective security controls at the design level — such as unrestricted field updates (mass assignment) or business logic that assumes trusted input.

test_patterns.name: Mass assignment of privileged fields
test_patterns.method: add extra, privileged fields (e.g. role, isAdmin, balance) to a write request that a normal user shouldn't be able to set
test_patterns.payload_template: Add "role": "admin" to a profile update payload

description: Missing security hardening, default credentials, verbose error handling, or unnecessary features/headers enabled, giving attackers extra information or attack surface.

test_patterns.name: Missing security headers
test_patterns.method: inspect response headers for Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, Content-Security-Policy
test_patterns.payload_template: Baseline GET request, inspect headers only

test_patterns.name: Version / stack disclosure
test_patterns.method: inspect Server / X-Powered-By headers for version strings
test_patterns.payload_template: Baseline GET request, inspect headers only

description: Use of libraries, frameworks, or components with known vulnerabilities, often revealed by version disclosure in headers or error pages.

test_patterns.name: Component version fingerprinting
test_patterns.method: collect framework/server version strings from headers and error pages to cross-reference against known CVEs
test_patterns.payload_template: Baseline GET request, inspect headers and error responses

description: Weaknesses in authentication flows — missing rate limiting on login, weak session handling, or predictable credentials — that allow account takeover.

test_patterns.name: Missing rate limiting on login
test_patterns.method: send repeated failed login attempts against a single account and check for lockout, CAPTCHA, or 429 responses
test_patterns.payload_template: Repeat POST /login with incorrect password N times in a short window

description: Code and infrastructure that does not verify integrity, such as accepting unsigned updates or deserializing untrusted data.

test_patterns.name: Unsigned/unverified payload acceptance
test_patterns.method: submit a payload with a missing or invalid integrity signature/checksum where one is expected
test_patterns.payload_template: Omit or corrupt an expected signature/checksum header

description: Insufficient logging, monitoring, or alerting means breaches and abuse go undetected for long periods.

test_patterns.name: No anomaly signal on abusive traffic
test_patterns.method: generate an obviously abusive traffic pattern (rapid repeated failed auth, scraping) and check for any observable throttling/alerting behavior
test_patterns.payload_template: Burst of requests in a short window, observe for 429/blocking behavior as a proxy for monitoring

description: The server fetches a remote resource based on user-supplied input without validating the destination, allowing attackers to reach internal services.

test_patterns.name: SSRF via user-supplied URL
test_patterns.method: supply an internal/loopback URL to any parameter that triggers a server-side fetch (webhooks, image-fetch, URL preview)
